definition: The consistent sequence in which a component calls ordinary Hooks during rendering. React relies on that sequence to associate each call with its stored information.
example: Call useState before a conditional return on every render.

definition: A Hook call made directly in a component or custom Hook body, before any conditional return. Ordinary Hooks cannot be called in branches, loops, event handlers or nested callbacks.
A function that calls React Hooks to package reusable behaviour. Its name starts with use followed by a capital letter; separate calls share the logic but do not automatically share local state.
example: Two calls to useCounter create independent counts.

definition: A code-checking tool configured with React rules to identify mistakes such as conditional Hook calls or missing reactive effect dependencies before the code runs.

An object whose current property can hold information between a component instance's renders. Changing current does not request a render, so refs are suited to non-display information and narrow DOM operations.
example: A ref can store a timer identifier for a later Stop handler.

definition: A React Hook that returns a persistent ref object with a mutable current property. Its initial argument supplies current on the initial render.
A ref attached to a rendered browser element so code can access its DOM object after commit. React sets the object ref's current property to that element and clears it when the element is removed.
example: An input ref lets a button handler focus that input.

definition: JavaScript's ?. syntax, which skips a property access or function call if the value being checked is null or undefined. It does not make every later operation or non-function value safe.
example: inputRef.current?.focus() skips the focus call if current is null.

definition: The browser's selection of the element that receives keyboard interaction. An element's focus method can move that selection to it when it is focusable.
A value returned when scheduling a browser timer, used to identify that timer when cancelling it. A ref can remember the identifier without making it part of rendered state.
A controlled way to work outside React's usual props-and-state rendering flow. Refs and effects allow necessary DOM access or external synchronisation while keeping most UI declarative.

React synchronisation logic declared with useEffect that runs after a component commits. It keeps an external system aligned with relevant component inputs and may return cleanup to stop the synchronisation.
A React Hook that declares external synchronisation using a setup function and optional dependency array. When dependencies change, React runs the previous cleanup before the next setup.
The function passed to useEffect that starts an external synchronisation. It can return a cleanup function to undo the work it started.
example: Setup registers a browser keydown listener.

definition: The function returned from an effect setup that stops or undoes that setup's work. React invokes it before replacing the effect after dependency changes and when removing the component.
example: Cleanup removes the exact callback that setup registered.

definition: Something outside React's rendering flow that a component needs to coordinate with, such as a browser event source or network connection. Effects can start and stop that coordination.
A callback registered on an event target to run when a particular event occurs. Removing it requires matching the event type, callback identity and capture setting.
An ongoing registration to receive external events. A component's effect can establish it and return cleanup that unregisters it when no longer needed.

A React development tool that adds checks for problems such as impure rendering and missing cleanup. When enabled at the root it includes an extra effect setup-and-cleanup cycle; these checks do not run in production.
Adding a component instance to the rendered tree. Its initial state is established, and its effects can start after commit.
Removing a component instance from the rendered tree. Its local state is discarded and React runs any current effect cleanup.
A fixed-length list of reactive inputs supplied to a Hook such as useEffect or useMemo. React compares each listed value using Object.is to decide whether the previous inputs still match.
example: An effect reading the room prop lists room as a dependency.

definition: A value from a component's rendering scope that may differ between renders, including props, state and local variables or functions. An effect must declare the reactive values it reads as dependencies.
A function still using values captured from an earlier render when current behaviour requires newer ones. Missing effect dependencies can keep an external subscription using obsolete inputs.
The browser interface for requesting resources asynchronously. fetch returns a Promise for a response and does not reject merely because the server sends an HTTP error status.
A JavaScript object representing the eventual success value or failure of an asynchronous operation. It can be pending before settling as fulfilled or rejected.
Work whose result may become available later, allowing other work to proceed while it is pending. An async JavaScript function returns a Promise and can use await to pause its own progress.
JavaScript syntax that pauses the current async function until a value or Promise settles. A fulfilled result becomes the expression's value; a rejection throws at that point for error handling.
A Fetch response property that is true for an HTTP status in the successful 200–299 range. Check it because an HTTP failure can still fulfil the fetch Promise.
A Fetch response method that reads the response body and returns a Promise for its parsed JSON value. Parsing can fail independently of the HTTP success status.
Running in the user's browser rather than on a server. Effects only run on the client, so the lesson's fetch starts after a browser commit.
A browser object that supplies a signal for cancelling supported asynchronous work such as fetch. Cancelling work differs from merely ignoring its eventual result.
A mechanism for supplying a value to descendant components without forwarding it through props at every layer. A consumer reads the nearest matching provider above it.

A React function called outside components to create a context object and a fallback value. The object identifies which information providers supply and consumers read; it does not own changing state itself.
A React Hook that reads and subscribes to the nearest matching context provider above its component. With no matching provider, it reads that context's default value.
An ancestor element that supplies a value for a particular React context to descendants. A nearer provider of that same context overrides a more distant provider.
A component that reads a context value, commonly by calling useContext. It receives updates when its relevant provider's value changes, even if the component is memoised.

A React wrapper that can skip a component's parent-driven rendering when its props are unchanged. It is a performance optimisation, not a guarantee, and does not stop the component's own state or context updates.
A React Hook that can reuse a pure calculation's result while its dependencies remain unchanged. The cache is an optimisation and may be discarded, so correctness must survive recalculation.
A React Hook that can reuse a function identity while its dependencies remain unchanged. It returns the function without invoking it, for example so an event handler can call it later.
A React Developer Tools panel for inspecting rendering performance. Use measurements of realistic interactions to identify costly work and compare attempted improvements.
Tools for inspecting a React application's components, props, state and performance. Browser extensions expose Components and Profiler panels.
A build-time tool that can automatically memoise React components, values and functions. It must be integrated into a supported project build; importing React alone does not enable it.

An integrated set of tools around React for building an application, often coordinating features such as routing and data loading. Its data facilities may handle work that a small teaching example implements manually with effects.
Producing HTML from React components on a server before the browser displays or interacts with the page. Effects do not run during this server work.
The name assistive technology uses to identify a user-interface element. Associating a visible label with an input can supply its accessible name.
Letting multiple consumers use the same pending request or result instead of sending equivalent duplicate requests. The lesson's manual fetch effect does not provide this feature.
Whether a text comparison treats upper- and lower-case letters as different. JavaScript string includes is case-sensitive; the task app lowercases both inputs before comparing to ignore letter case.

Whether two values refer to the same function or object rather than newly created ones with similar code or fields. React's Object.is comparisons treat a newly created function, object or array as different.
A JavaScript statement that runs a try block and transfers control to a catch block if that work throws an error. A rejected Promise awaited inside the try block is caught there too.
A JavaScript constructor that creates an object describing an error, commonly with a message. Creating an Error object does not throw it; throw starts the error-handling path.
example: throw new Error("Request failed") creates an error and throws it.

definition: JavaScript object-literal syntax that uses a variable name as both the property name and the source of its value. It avoids repeating the name on both sides of a colon.
example: { count, increment } means { count: count, increment: increment }.
